record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.context_brief: Non-perturbative QCD and soft hadronic reactions
record.original_question: How can high-energy soft hadronic reactions be understood from the non-perturbative behavior of quantum field theory, especially QCD confinement, where the vacuum shifts from elementary quark and gluon fields to hadrons and the usual perturbative treatment is beyond reach?

evidence.quote: "Soft Physics", at least when concerning elementary particles, appears really as the "Hard Problem".

We remain thus far from a deep understanding of "soft" hadronic reactions at high energy which implies a knowledge of the non-perturbative behaviour of Quantum Field Theory. More precisely the confinement problem in QCD, which requires a non-perturbative vacuum shift from the elementary quark and gluon fields to hadrons, is for the moment beyond reach. So, what to do?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Within the framework of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), a non-abelian SU(3) gauge theory of quark fields coupled to gluons, develop a theoretical description of high-energy soft hadronic reactions (i.e. hadron–hadron scattering processes dominated by small momentum transfer, where the QCD coupling is large and standard perturbative expansions in the coupling do not converge) directly from the non-perturbative dynamics of the underlying quantum field theory. In particular, account for color confinement, understood as a non-perturbative rearrangement of the QCD vacuum in which the asymptotic physical states are color-singlet hadrons rather than the elementary quark and gluon fields, and derive from this picture the observed phenomenology of soft high-energy scattering (total and elastic cross sections, diffractive amplitudes, multiparticle production, and intermittency-type fluctuations in particle distributions).
artifact.status_search_result: Color confinement and a first-principles non-perturbative derivation of soft high-energy hadronic scattering from QCD remain unsolved. The mass gap / confinement problem for Yang–Mills theory is one of the Clay Millennium Prize Problems and is still open; soft-QCD phenomenology continues to rely on models (Regge/Pomeron, stochastic vacuum, holographic QCD) rather than a rigorous non-perturbative derivation.

status_evidence.title: Yang–Mills and Mass Gap
status_evidence.snippet: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap.
status_evidence.claim: The non-perturbative behavior of Yang–Mills/QCD, including confinement, is officially recognized as an open problem.
